profile.title: From systems & networks to Salesforce development
profile.p1: Salesforce developer with 2 years of professional experience and a strong IT infrastructure background — foundations that make a real difference on complex projects.
profile.p2: I started my career on the infrastructure side — internship at MIDRANGE GROUP (Feb – May 2023) as a junior systems & network administrator: support for 50+ workstations, deployment of 200 Dell machines via Windows Autopilot, Windows Server 2022 administration (AD DS, DNS, DHCP, GPO), PfSense/Squid, Acronis, Datto RMM. This hands-on experience taught me how systems behave in real life and why solid foundations matter.
profile.p3: From Oct. 2023 to Oct. 2025, I worked as a Salesforce Developer at LD Digitales (remote) while earning the Développeur Concepteur Logiciel title (RNCP Level 6) from OpenClassrooms. I built and maintained 10+ Apex classes, created 20+ automation Flows (reducing manual workload by 30%), designed reusable LWC components, and implemented CI/CD pipelines with Salesforce CLI.
profile.p4: I do my best work in environments that value autonomy, transparency, and continuous learning. My goal is to contribute to ambitious Salesforce and IT Ops projects — in France or internationally, within distributed teams.
profile.p1_salesforce: Salesforce developer & consultant: I design reliable, secure, maintainable solutions with a strong focus on user experience and delivery quality.
profile.p2_salesforce: I work with Apex, Flows, data models, security (permission sets, sharing), and CI/CD pipelines (Salesforce CLI, GitHub Actions) to ship cleanly to production.
profile.p3_salesforce: My systems & DevOps background helps me approach Salesforce with an operations mindset: observability, risk management, documentation, and automation—so solutions stay robust over time.
profile.p4_salesforce: Full-time Salesforce Developer at LD Digitales since October 2025, with 2 years of production Salesforce experience — alongside building two Salesforce SaaS products (OrgDocs and SFRelease). The Legarant-AXG project (Heroku Connect, environment management, traceable production releases) remains the clearest proof of that Salesforce/infra crossover: not an application layer sitting on infrastructure someone else manages, but the same person on both sides.
profile.p1_itops: IT Ops & DevOps: I help teams design, maintain, and secure resilient infrastructure, with pragmatic operations processes (runbooks, monitoring, remediation).
profile.p2_itops: I implement operations standards: actionable monitoring/alerting, noise reduction, escalation procedures, documentation, and automation (scripts, jobs, playbooks).
profile.p3_itops: I pay close attention to security and continuity: backups, hardening, access management, and change practices to reduce incidents.
profile.p4_itops: Full-time Salesforce Developer at LD Digitales — IT Ops & DevOps skills, built through real production environments, remain fully available for targeted projects.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know before reaching out.

items.a: Yes, I'm available immediately. I'm currently working as a Salesforce Developer at LD Digitales, and I'm open to permanent, fixed-term, freelance, and contract roles — in France and internationally. For roles requiring a Salesforce certification (Administrator), my effective availability is around September 2026, once I've obtained it. Feel free to reach out to discuss your needs.

Yes — full remote, hybrid, or on-site depending on your needs. I'm based in Marseille / Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur and open to relocation in France and internationally: Belgium, Luxembourg, Germany, Italy, Spain, UK, Ireland, Malta, and any English-speaking context. Video calls, async communication, and documented handovers are part of my standard workflow.

It depends on the scope. A Salesforce audit or a focused feature (Flow, Apex class) usually takes 1–5 days. A full implementation with testing and documentation typically runs 2–8 weeks. I'll give you a precise estimate after an initial scoping call — no commitment required.

items.q: How does a typical engagement work?
items.a: It usually goes like this: a short discovery call (30 min) to understand your context → a written proposal with scope, deliverables, and timeline → delivery with clear documentation → a handover session so your team can maintain everything independently. You own all the code and configuration I produce.

items.q: Do you offer support after delivery?
items.a: Yes. I include a short support window after each delivery for adjustments and questions. For ongoing maintenance or feature evolution, we can discuss a retainer arrangement.

accessibility.helpBody: If you encounter a barrier while navigating this website — element not reachable by keyboard, missing image alternative, insufficient contrast, or any other difficulty — please report it by specifying the URL of the page and the nature of the problem.
